Duration API Reference¶

Back to PlussQit API Reference

This page documents pluss::Duration and pluss::codeh::Duration in the same handwritten reference style used for Series, Note, Timeline, and TimeIndex: fixed layout, one method page at a time, richer prose, verified outputs, and practical emphasis over autogenerated signature dumps.

What Duration Is¶

Duration is the elapsed-time payload object in PlussQit — the counterpart to Timeline’s instants.

Where Timeline answers “when” (canonical storage: epoch nanoseconds in UTC), Duration answers “how long” (canonical storage: elapsed nanoseconds, with no anchor to any calendar date). This is the same split as std::chrono::time_point vs. std::chrono::duration, or Python’s datetime.datetime vs. datetime.timedelta.

Duration is a genuine standalone N-D array type, not a helper that only exists inside a Timeline expression — it has its own shape (dim(), numel(), sizes()), its own factories (including range(), which builds an array with no Timeline involved at all), and a full arithmetic/comparison/ conversion surface. The one real asymmetry: Duration is not one of the four ThreadKind payloads a DataFrame column can hold (Series, Note, Timeline, TimeIndex) — to store elapsed time in a column, convert to a plain Series first via one of the total() accessor’s unit methods.

Important

Build with CODEH_ENABLE_DURATION_SURFACE defined Duration’s generated method surface (every comparison, mul/div/floordiv/ mod, total()’s unit conversions, abs/sign/clip, isnat/fill_nat/where) is compiled in only when CODEH_ENABLE_DURATION_SURFACE is defined, mirroring how Timeline’s and TimeIndex’s surfaces are gated behind their own flags. PlussQit’s own plussqit_codeh CMake target now defines it (alongside CODEH_ENABLE_TIMELINE_SURFACE/CODEH_ENABLE_TIMEINDEX_SURFACE), so anything linking against PlussQit::CodeH gets it automatically. If you see Duration missing methods like total() or operator* in a different build target, this define is the first thing to check.

Use Duration when you have elapsed time that isn’t anchored to a particular calendar date:

  • the result of Timeline - Timeline

  • an offset to add to or subtract from a Timeline (t + Duration)

  • a fixed-width step for building a regular sequence (pluss::duration::range)

  • a magnitude to compare, scale, or convert to a human unit

Use Timeline’s own calendar-unit methods (add_months, add_years, add_days, not yet on their own reference page) instead when the operation should respect calendar irregularities (a month isn’t a fixed number of days) — Duration arithmetic is always a fixed nanosecond offset, with no awareness of month length or leap years. Timeline::add_duration is the Duration-based sibling documented here.

Note

Duration (capital D) is the type; pluss::duration (lowercase) is its factory Construction lives in its own namespace, kept separate from the type itself — the same split as pluss::timeline::make/pluss::timeline::from_epoch being separate from Timeline. pluss::duration::seconds(5), not pluss::duration_seconds(5); pluss::duration::range(...), not pluss::timedelta_range(...). See construction for the full factory surface.

Includes¶

#include <pluss/pluss.h>
// or the narrower temporal surface
#include <pluss/codeh/codeh.h>
#include <pluss/codeh/duration_factory.h>
// timeline_factory.h also includes duration_factory.h transitively, since
// Timeline arithmetic consumes Duration -- but Duration does not depend on
// Timeline, so duration_factory.h stands alone as its own header.

Practical Construction Patterns¶

Example 1. The friendly unit factories — the normal way to build a scalar Duration.

auto ninety_min = pluss::duration::minutes(90);
auto one_hour = pluss::duration::hours(1);
auto one_day = pluss::duration::days(1);
auto neg_fifteen_min = pluss::duration::minutes(-15);

Negative counts are valid and mean “backward in time” — see abs for recovering a magnitude.

Example 2. Every unit factory also builds 1D and N-D arrays — not just scalars — the same three ways pluss::timeline::make does.

auto one_d = pluss::duration::minutes({15, 30, 45, 60});          // 1D, 4 elements
auto nested_2d = pluss::duration::hours({{1, 2}, {3, 4}, {5, 6}}); // 2D, shape [3,2]

Explicit flat-plus-shape construction is also available for any rank, mirroring pluss::timeline::from_epoch(flat, sizes) — plain braces convert implicitly to pluss::RangeView<int64_t>, no explicit wrapping needed:

auto explicit_2x2 = pluss::duration::days({1, 2, 3, 4}, {2, 2});

Example 3. pluss::duration::make(values, unit) — the same construction surface again, with the unit picked at runtime via pluss::duration::Unit instead of by function name (Unit::Nanos, ::Seconds, ::Minutes, ::Hours, ::Days, ::Weeks, ::Microseconds, ::Milliseconds).

auto d = pluss::duration::make(5'400, pluss::duration::Unit::Seconds);
// equivalently: pluss::duration::seconds(5'400);

Example 4. A regular sequence of durations, with no Timeline involved.

auto steps = pluss::duration::range(
    pluss::duration::days(0), pluss::duration::days(10), pluss::duration::days(2));
// steps.dim() == 1, steps.numel() == 6

Example 5. As the byproduct of subtracting two Timelines.

auto gap = end_timeline - start_timeline;  // pluss::Duration

Coverage¶

This reference covers the canonical public surface:

  • construction: pluss::duration::nanos/seconds/minutes/hours/days (each with scalar, 1D, nested-N-D, and flat+shape overloads), pluss::duration::range

  • arithmetic: add, sub, neg, mul, div, floordiv, mod

  • comparisons (elementwise, return Series[bool]): eq, ne, lt, le, gt, ge

  • unary transforms: abs, sign, clip

  • unit conversion (all return a plain Series): total().nanoseconds(), total().microseconds(), total().milliseconds(), total().seconds(), total().minutes(), total().hours(), total().days(), total().weeks()

  • missing-value handling: isnat, isvalid, fill_nat, where

  • Timeline integration: Timeline ± Duration, Timeline - Timeline

Each distinct method has its own page — matching the convention used by PlussMic’s DataFrame reference. A true one-line alias with zero behavior difference from its canonical method (isfinite()/isnan(), for example) is documented on that canonical method’s page rather than getting a near-empty page of its own; every other method, including ones that share an implementation pattern with a sibling (the six comparisons, the eight total_* unit accessors), gets its own page.

Using This Reference¶

  • Use the left sidebar to open one Duration method page at a time.

  • Each page embeds verified output directly under the example that produced it, captured from PlussQit/examples/CodeH/duration_docverify_demo.cpp.

  • A true one-line alias (isfinite()/isnan()) is documented on its canonical method’s page rather than getting a page of its own — see that page’s Notes section for the alias.
